judgment_round: 7th independent verdict on implementation_steps 10-13 (4th, 5th and 6th were all fail)
fail_reasons: AC-11/SC-9 violated: 26 of 60 mechanically generated brace notations that genuinely expand to a control-plane path are allow (no prompt). 10 proven end-to-end by actually deleting the file in an isolated lab, plus 1 proven overwrite via tee.

Class E is a NEW regression from this round's own parser: 600 unmatched '{' in a delete operand costs 5.26s against the 5s hook timeout (hooks/hooks.json:26); 4096 chars — exactly at the new length cap — costs 517s. Baseline 142d737 was 0.27s on the same input.

what_this_round_did_fix_verified_indepen.6th_verdict_Class_A_degenerate_range: CLOSED. 65bdce7 allow -> 42e04ec ask on all of: `rm -rf .clau{d..d}e`, `rm -rf .claude/setting{s..s}.json`, `rm -rf .claude/hook{s..s}`.
what_this_round_did_fix_verified_indepen.range_parser_correctness: Zero-padding, reverse ranges, explicit step, step 0, >15-digit overflow and mixed forms (`{1..a}`) all behave as designed; unrecognized dot-dot forms fail closed to ask. Checked against real bash expansion, not just against the code.
what_this_round_did_fix_verified_indepen.over_blocking: No regression. A 20-case battery (node_modules, dist/*, build/{js,css}, backup{1..5}, src/hooks, web/src/hooks, coverage/{...}, out/{1..10}, find -delete, ...) is identical to the 142d737 baseline — 0 deltas.
what_this_round_did_fix_verified_indepen.assessment: Both fixes are principled rather than ad hoc: the range count is computed arithmetically before any value is materialised, and the glob fold was genuinely relocated to after expansion rather than special-cased. Credit is due for both, and for the honest disclosure of the residual 6.8s.

issues.title: [security] normalize_path_token() runs once BEFORE brace expansion and is never re-applied to the expanded candidates — any path component the expansion re-introduces ('.', '//', trailing '/') defeats the gate
issues.root_cause: hooks/pre-bash-firewall.sh: scan_control_plane_delete() calls normalize_path_token "$tok" (:1187) then control_plane_location "$NORM_TOK" (:1199). Inside __control_plane_location_impl the recursion reconstructs "${pre}${item}${post}" (:1052, :1066) and re-enters the function directly — the reconstructed string never passes through normalize_path_token again. So '//' collapsing, '/./' folding and trailing-'/' stripping only ever apply to the UNEXPANDED token.
repro_commands: rm -rf {.claude/,zz}                     # bash -> '.claude/' == .claude        -> allow, DELETES the whole .claude dir
rm -rf .claude/{.,zz}/settings.json      # bash -> '.claude/./settings.json'    -> allow, DELETES the wiring file
rm -rf hooks/{.,zz}/hooks.json           # bash -> 'hooks/./hooks.json'         -> allow, DELETES hooks.json
tee .claude/{zz,.}/settings.json < /tmp/evil.json   # -> allow, OVERWRITES the wiring file (verified mutated)
issues.evidence: Isolated labs under /tmp/f65lab*: each command judged first, then executed; target went present -> DELETED. Same allow on rm / mv / unlink / shred (rmdir happens to be caught by an unrelated pattern).
issues.why_it_matters: `.claude/` is gitignored (.gitignore:9) so protected-integrity.sh has no HEAD baseline — these deletions are unrecoverable. This is precisely the class AC-11/SC-9 exists for.
issues.note: Present in 142d737, e2be94e, 65bdce7 and 42e04ec alike — not introduced this round — but squarely on the brace-expansion axis this round claims to have closed, and `rm -rf {.claude/,zz}` is one character away from the contract's own step-10 example.

issues.title: [security] a brace group containing a quoted space is torn apart by the token splitter before quotes are handled, so the group is never seen as a group
issues.root_cause: scan_control_plane_delete() splits with `read -r -a toks <<<"$seg"` (:1177), i.e. on raw whitespace, while normalize_path_token strips quotes only afterwards (:838). bash removes quotes AFTER brace expansion, so `{.claude,'a b'}` is one word to bash and two to the firewall — both halves have unbalanced braces and fall through as literals.
repro_commands: rm -rf {.claude,'a b'}           # bash -> '.claude' 'a b'  -> allow, DELETES .claude
rm -rf hooks/{hooks.json,'a b'}  # -> allow, DELETES hooks/hooks.json
issues.evidence: Isolated lab /tmp/f65labD.*: all three judged allow, then executed; targets deleted.
issues.note: Also present in all four commits.

issues.title: [security][perf] NEW REGRESSION — __brace_find_group() is O(n^2) in token length, and the 4096-char cap admits the worst case (517s) instead of bounding it
issues.root_cause: hooks/pre-bash-firewall.sh:934-948. When a '{' has no matching '}', the loop does `start=$((i+1)); continue` and rescans to the end of the token looking for the next '{'. With n unmatched braces that is sum(n-i) = O(n^2) pure-bash character reads. __BRACE_BUDGET never fires on this path because no group is ever successfully found, so the budget cannot bound it. The 4096-char cap (:1026) bounds LENGTH, not the number of scan restarts.

measurements_hook_timeout_is_5s.4200 open braces (over the cap): 0.28s ask — the cap works, but it is set above the worst case

issues.regression_proof: Same input (512 '{'), per version: 142d737 0.27s / e2be94e 0.32s / 65bdce7 4.95s / 42e04ec 4.73s. With a NON-arming verb (`echo`) at HEAD the same 512-char token costs 0.26s — so the cost lives entirely inside the control-plane delete brace parser, not in the general per-length firewall cost.
issues.exploit_shape: `rm -rf {{{{...(>=600) .claude` measures 5.26s and WOULD return ask, but only after the 5s timeout in hooks/hooks.json:26 has killed the hook, so the decision never reaches the harness. This is the same failure mode the 5th verdict rejected (16 sequential groups -> 22.7s), re-opened through a different construction.
issues.caveat: I did not directly observe Claude Code's behaviour on hook timeout. I am applying this project's own already-accepted criterion — the 5th verdict treated exceeding the 5s timeout as a bypass, and the implementer's report uses the same framing.
issues.suggested_fix: Bound the scan, not just the length: a single left-to-right pass with a stack finds every balanced group in O(n) without restarts; or count '{' first and fail closed above a small constant.

issues.title: [docs] docs/INVARIANTS.md asserts a bound that does not hold
issues.detail: The INV-14 section added in this commit says of __BRACE_BUDGET: '이 반환이 호출 스택을 타고 전파돼 형제 분기를 펴지 않으므로 총 작업량이 예산에 비례해 유계다' (total work is bounded proportionally to the budget). Class E is not bounded by the budget — the budget is never decremented on that path. The neighbouring claim that the 4096-char cap handles the length-proportional cost is also wrong in effect: within the cap the cost is quadratic and reaches 517s. This repeats the repository's own recurring 'docs stronger than code' pattern (progress/lessons.md:511, :803, :847).

issues.title: [test] step 13's combination generator enumerates notation axes but never COMPOSES them — the one thing it was added to do
issues.detail: tests/pre-bash-firewall.bats:2483-2513 iterates target x notation x verb over four independent notations (plain, quoted, brace, dotslash). Its own comment says the point is '축의 교차에서만 드러나는 조합' (combinations visible only where axes cross), but notate_brace and notate_dotslash are applied alternatively, never together. Composing exactly those two existing axes reproduces Class C immediately: `rm -rf ./.claude/{./,unused/}settings.json` -> allow, `rm -rf ./hooks/{./,unused/}hooks.json` -> allow. Contract step 13 is marked done:true, but its _done_note substantiates only the protected-integrity SC-8 half; the AC-11 generator half is unmet.

issues.title: [test] the new perf test is calibrated below both the real risk and the real timeout
issues.detail: tests/pre-bash-firewall.bats:2424-2437 uses 3000 commas with a 3000ms bound, while the hook's actual timeout is 5000ms and the implementer's own disclosed failing case (10000 commas, 6.86s) is larger than what the test exercises. No test covers scan-restart cost (Class E) at all.

issues.title: [process] no implementer-output JSON was produced for this round
issues.detail: progress/agent-comms/ holds implementer-output-F72/F73/F74 but nothing for this F65 round; the self-check reached the evaluator only through the dispatch prompt. The evaluator contract expects implementer-output.json carrying security_self_check and criteria_backfill.

issues.title: [method] any differential harness written for this repo must avoid `mapfile`
issues.detail: Not a defect in the code under review. Recording it because my own first differential silently reported zero findings on macOS bash 3.2 (no mapfile) — exactly the failure mode that would let a round pass on an empty test. Future generators should assert that the generator itself produced a non-zero number of checked cases.

scope_judgment_on_residual_performance.question: Is the disclosed residual 6.8s inside or outside F65's scope?
scope_judgment_on_residual_performance.answer: Split — the implementer's framing is half right.
scope_judgment_on_residual_performance.measured_10k_comma_case: 142d737 11.93s / e2be94e 20.20s / 65bdce7 74.81s / 42e04ec 6.86s. Same-length non-arming verb: 1.80s at HEAD, 1.65s at 142d737.
scope_judgment_on_residual_performance.out_of_scope_part: For THAT input the implementer is broadly correct — most of the cost predates this round (142d737 was already 11.9s, itself over the timeout) and ~1.8s is genuinely the general per-length firewall cost. Their change is a real ~10x improvement there. That general per-length cost belongs to a separate feature, not to F65.
scope_judgment_on_residual_performance.in_scope_part: The claim that `control_plane_location()` itself is negligible (0.01s) does not generalise. For the unmatched-brace class it is the ENTIRE cost (0.26s non-arming vs 4.73s armed at the same length), it is newly introduced by this round's parser, and it is far worse (517s at the cap). That part is unambiguously inside F65's scope and is a fail reason.

root_cause_assessment_round_7.recorded_lesson: progress/lessons.md:1245 — '판정이 지목한 반례 목록을 통과시키는 것과 그 반례가 속한 축을 닫는 것은 다르다' (making the listed counterexamples pass is not the same as closing the axis they belong to).
root_cause_assessment_round_7.did_this_round_follow_it: Partly. The two named classes were repaired at the mechanism level rather than by pattern-matching the specific strings, and those repairs hold under independent test.
root_cause_assessment_round_7.but: The method that produces the recurrence was not applied. The lesson prescribes mechanically differencing against real shell expansion; the round verified the two counterexamples it was handed plus hand-picked neighbours. A 60-template generator built from the contract's OWN notation axes took minutes to write and found 26 ungated forms — including one (`rm -rf {.claude/,zz}`) a single character from the contract's own step-10 example. Composing the two notations the existing bats generator already contains reproduces the bypass directly.
root_cause_assessment_round_7.conclusion: Seventh round, same structural cause intact: the axis is closed case-by-case rather than by construction. The remedy is not another counterexample list — it is a differential test that expands every generated token with real bash, canonicalises each resulting word, and asserts at-least-ask whenever any word resolves to a control-plane path. Such a test would have caught C and D, and with a wall-clock assertion, E — before this dispatch.

missing_criteria: No acceptance criterion states that the judgment must AGREE WITH REAL SHELL EXPANSION — every round so far restates a list of notations. AC-11 should be rewritten as a property: 'for any operand token, if any word bash expands it to canonicalises to a control-plane path, the verdict is at least ask.'
No criterion bounds the firewall's own decision latency against the 5s hook timeout. Two rounds have now failed on latency and it is still not a written criterion.
ambiguous_criteria: step 13's '조합 생성기(동사 × 대상 × 표기 축)' does not say whether notation axes must COMPOSE; the implementation read it as alternation, which is why the test is green while the bypass is open.
security_criteria_insufficient: SC-9 covers deletion only. The same notation defeats the write arms (tee proven to overwrite). SC-9 or a sibling criterion should cover any control-plane mutation verb, not just deletion.
criteria_gaps.action_required: Before the next implementation round, rewrite AC-11 as a shell-expansion-agreement property and add a latency criterion tied to the 5s timeout; only then re-open implementation_steps 10-13.
